captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a customizable landing gear adapter for multi-copters, designed to connect two square tubes at a 45-degree angle. It features a horizontal square socket and a second square socket angled downwards at 45 degrees, merged into a single structural piece with a triangular truss-like cutout in the center for weight reduction. Two small cylindrical screw holes are positioned on the side walls to secure the inserted tubes in place.
captions.instruction: Design a customizable landing gear adapter in OpenSCAD that can switch between an 'adapter' and a 'stopper' part. The adapter should connect two square tubes at a 45-degree angle using a structural truss, with parameters for shaft length, inner tube diameter, wall thickness, and screw hole diameter.
captions.factory: The design uses a selector module 'choose_part()' to toggle between the 'adapter' and 'landing' (stopper) modules. The 'adapter' module constructs the outer geometry by applying 'hull()' over two square profiles (one horizontal and one rotated 45 degrees around the Y-axis) defined in the 'outlines' helper module. It then subtracts a scaled-down version of the hull to hollow out the truss area, subtracts the inner square cavities using 'outlines(true)', and finally subtracts rotated cylindrical screw holes.
